paragraphs: Leica cameras have this magic that pulls you in. I love it. I went for a medium-distance walk from my home to Ikebukuro, which felt like about three to three and a half hours.

That was quite good. Somehow, I ended up on some streets I had already been to, but most of them were new. I found a few cute places, perhaps found an old abandoned Rolls-Royce somewhere in the northern part, and also a few cute neighborhoods.
It was a good reminder of how nice walking is and how pleasant it usually is.

walks.summary: A walk toward Ikebukuro, discovering new streets, small neighborhoods and a possibly abandoned Rolls-Royce.

paragraphs: I was supposed to take a long walk around the northern part of the Aurelian Walls, but surprise, surprise, only 200-400 meters of it remain near Roma Termini.
I walked the whole part from Alsmots St. Peter (from Gianicolo Museum) to the Tiber and then some more along the shore.
Two and a half rolls later, I ended up at Ponte Sisto.

walks.summary: A west-wall walk after discovering how little of the northern wall remains, finishing near Ponte Sisto.

paragraphs: I had fairly short, but very hot, walk around Aurelian Walls around Rome.
Somehow I ended up at Colosseum after walking up the street next to east gate — Porta Metronia. I didn’t use maps for walking as I was following the wall.

Somewhere I in first roll of this three-roll walk I started to shoot things in front of the Aurelian Walls — some shots don’t have wall at all. Although there was a bit of where what was in front of the wall — were other walls — mostly of expensive villas or private land. Some wall with torn cloth (?) were a funny contrast to the actual AWs.

walks.summary: Following Rome’s Aurelian Walls without a map and photographing what stands in front of them.

paragraphs: Today was third Osanpo (お散歩) since I started to schedule those a month or so ago. I took train to Ochanomizu and headed to Mizumoto Park. It is not a momiji season yet, but I was curious to see the park and akso it was in a direction I never walked.

That part of Tokyo is quite interesting. Main streets have very near-looking corners and cozy aura around them. Residential areas are also extremely warm and scenic (but not in an European way). There are bits of the city, specially further north—that looks completly like suburbs: very wide streets, big houses, quite low density of everything.
Katsushika is one of those wards I have never visited before. It looks like Adachi, but not a Kita-Senju.

walks.summary: The third scheduled Osanpo heads toward Mizumoto Park, exploring unfamiliar parts of Katsushika.

paragraphs: Totally by accident walks near UNPLAN Kagurazaka Caffe (from my Cafés in Tokyo list). One could say it was an unplanned stop, heh. They ave some amazing coffee and very generous lunch menu portions. Definitely will be coming here for work in future. Good find. Ok, time to move forwards.
Arrived at Rec Coffee near industrial and quite interesting complex of bridges and infrastructure in Suidobashi (of of those bridges is Suidobashi, I think).
They sell a lot of coffee blends. Kissa blend cough my eye—I might even get one. It's marked as extremely bitter. Curious what kind of fire it'll become in AeroPress.

walks.summary: An unplanned stop at UNPLAN Kagurazaka, then Rec Coffee and the bridges around Suidobashi.

paragraphs: I somehow managed to walk from Harajuku to Ginza by feet. Tokyo suddenly seems tad smaller. All fo this was part of the photowalk with couple of art galleries in between. Overall, good day.

I have problem with my photos though. I don’t like anything I shoot. It’s not like I’m bored with photography. Quite the opposite, I’m itching to go out and shoot, but I’m bored with a type of photos I make. Something has to click, and I’m looking for it.

walks.summary: A photo walk from Harajuku to Ginza with art galleries along the way.

paragraphs: I walked for at least four hours from Nishi-Niporri all the way to Akihabara, going through Yanaka and Ueno. I have not seen photos yet, but I do not have high hopes. Very few people were roaming those streets to take photos of. Yet, I enjoyed walks a lot; It was calm and relaxing.
